subject: science
title: KS3 / Year 7-9 Science — Physics Waves
subtitle: Revision pack covering wave properties, sound, light, reflection, refraction, the electromagnetic spectrum and practical skills.
description: A KS3 physics revision pack about waves as energy transfers. It covers mechanical and electromagnetic waves, sound and light, wave properties, reflection, refraction, the electromagnetic spectrum, practical investigations and common misconceptions.

data.sentence: A wave transfers ____ without transferring matter overall.
data.hint: It is what can move from source to receiver.

data.sentence: Sound cannot travel through a ____ because there are no particles to vibrate.
data.hint: Space is almost one.

data.sentence: A mechanical wave needs a material ____ to travel through.
data.hint: Air can be one for sound.

data.sentence: Light from the Sun reaches Earth because electromagnetic waves can travel through a ____.
data.hint: Sound cannot do this.

data.sentence: In a transverse wave, vibrations are at ____ angles to the direction of energy transfer.
data.hint: Think 90 degrees.

data.sentence: In a longitudinal wave, vibrations are ____ to the direction of energy transfer.
data.hint: Sound is the key example.

data.sentence: The highest point of a transverse wave is a ____.
data.hint: It is the top of the wave.

data.sentence: The lowest point of a transverse wave is a ____.
data.hint: It is below the rest position.

data.sentence: A region where particles are close together in a sound wave is a ____.
data.hint: Particles are squeezed together.

data.sentence: The distance from one crest to the next crest is the ____.
data.hint: It is a length, not a height.

data.sentence: The maximum displacement from the rest position is the ____.
data.hint: For sound, increasing it usually makes the sound louder.

data.sentence: The number of vibrations each second is called ____.
data.hint: It is measured in hertz.

data.sentence: A sound with a higher frequency has a higher ____.
data.hint: This is about high or low sound.

data.sentence: A sound with a larger amplitude usually sounds ____.
data.hint: Amplitude is not the same as pitch.

data.sentence: An echo is a ____ sound wave.
data.hint: It bounces back from a surface.

data.sentence: We see a non-luminous book when light ____ from the book into the eye.
data.hint: The eye does not send out sight rays.

data.sentence: A material that transmits light clearly is ____.
data.hint: Clear glass is an example.

data.sentence: A material that scatters transmitted light so images are blurred is ____.
data.hint: Frosted glass is an example.

data.sentence: A shadow forms when an ____ object blocks light.
data.hint: This kind of material does not transmit light.

data.sentence: In reflection, angles are measured from the ____.
data.hint: This line is at 90 degrees to the surface.

data.sentence: The law of reflection states that angle of incidence ____ angle of reflection.
data.hint: The two angles are the same size.

data.sentence: Refraction happens when a wave changes direction at a boundary because its ____ changes.
data.hint: The ray bends when it enters a different material.

data.sentence: When light enters glass from air, it slows down and usually bends ____ the normal.
data.hint: Leaving glass for air is the opposite.

data.sentence: The electromagnetic spectrum order begins with radio waves and ends with ____ rays.
data.hint: These have the highest frequency in the KS3 order.

data.sentence: Radio waves are ____ waves, not sound waves.
data.hint: They can travel through a vacuum.

data.sentence: Microwaves heat food but do not make it ____.
data.hint: This is a common misconception.

data.sentence: The variable deliberately changed in an investigation is the ____ variable.
data.hint: It goes on the x-axis in many graphs.

data.sentence: The variable measured in an investigation is the ____ variable.
data.hint: It depends on what was changed.

data.sentence: A result that does not fit the pattern is called an ____ result.
data.hint: It should be checked, not simply ignored.

data.sentence: Repeating readings and calculating a mean can improve ____.
data.hint: This makes evidence more trustworthy.

data.title: How a sound wave reaches an ear
data.instruction: Put the stages of sound transfer in the correct order.
items: A source object vibrates.
Nearby air particles are pushed and pulled.
Compressions and rarefactions travel through the air.
Air particles vibrate backwards and forwards around their positions.
The sound energy reaches the ear.
The ear detects the vibration as sound.

data.title: Seeing a non-luminous object
data.instruction: Put the steps for seeing a book in the correct order.
items: A luminous object such as a lamp gives out light.
Light travels from the lamp to the book.
The non-luminous book reflects some of the light.
Reflected light travels from the book into the eye.
The eye detects the light and information about the book.

data.title: Drawing a reflection ray diagram
data.instruction: Put the ray diagram steps in the correct order.
items: Draw the plane mirror as a straight line.
Mark the point where the incident ray hits the mirror.
Draw the normal at 90 degrees to the mirror.
Measure the angle between the incident ray and the normal.
Draw the reflected ray on the other side of the normal with the same angle.
Add arrowheads and labels for the rays and angles.

data.title: Refraction through a rectangular glass block
data.instruction: Put the refraction stages in the correct order.
items: Light travels through air towards the glass block.
At the air-glass boundary the light slows down.
The ray bends towards the normal as it enters the glass.
The ray travels straight through the uniform glass.
At the glass-air boundary the light speeds up.
The ray bends away from the normal and emerges parallel to the incident ray.

data.title: Sound level and distance investigation
data.instruction: Put the practical method in the correct order.
items: Set the speaker to a steady tone at a safe volume.
Place the sound level meter at the first measured distance.
Record the sound level in decibels.
Repeat readings at the same distance.
Repeat the method for larger distances.
Calculate means and plot distance against mean sound level.
